tool.name: CITE-Seq Analysis
tool.description: Analyze pre-QC'ed RNA and raw ADT data from CITE-Seq experiments
tool.command:
python '$__tool_directory__/cite_seq_analysis.py'
#if $input_type.input_source == "separate" --rna-input '$input_type.rna_input' --adt-input '$input_type.adt_input' #else --mudata-input '$input_type.mudata_input' #end if
--rna-min-genes $qc.rna_min_genes --rna-min-cells $qc.rna_min_cells --max-mito-pct $qc.max_mito_pct --mito-prefix '$qc.mito_prefix' --adt-min-counts $qc.adt_min_counts
--adt-norm-method $normalization.adt_norm_method
#if $normalization.adt_norm_method == "dsb" and $normalization.use_isotype_control --use-isotype-control #if $normalization.isotype_controls --isotype-controls #for control in str($normalization.isotype_controls).split(',') '${control.strip()}' #end for #end if #end if
--rna-target-sum $normalization.rna_target_sum
#if $normalization.normalize_rna --normalize-rna #end if
--raw-counts-location $normalization.raw_counts_location --raw-counts-layer '$normalization.raw_counts_layer'
--hvg-min-mean $rna_processing.hvg_min_mean --hvg-max-mean $rna_processing.hvg_max_mean --hvg-min-disp $rna_processing.hvg_min_disp --scale-max-value $rna_processing.scale_max_value --n-pcs $rna_processing.n_pcs
--integration-method $integration.integration_method
#if $integration.integration_method == "totalVI" --n-latent $integration.n_latent --max-epochs $integration.max_epochs --gpu-device $integration.gpu_device #if $integration.batch_key --batch-key '$integration.batch_key' #end if #if $integration.continuous_covariates --continuous-covariates #for cov in str($integration.continuous_covariates).strip().split('\n') '${cov.strip()}' #end for #end if #if $integration.categorical_covariates --categorical-covariates #for cov in str($integration.categorical_covariates).strip().split('\n') '${cov.strip()}' #end for #end if #end if
--integrated-dim-reduction-key '$integration.integrated_dim_reduction_key'
--n-neighbors $clustering.n_neighbors --resolution $clustering.resolution --umap-min-dist $clustering.umap_min_dist
--output-format $output.output_format --output-file '$output_file'

param.name: rna_min_genes
param.label: Minimum number of genes per cell for RNA
param.help: Only used for joint QC if needed, assuming RNA is pre-QC'ed

param.name: rna_min_cells
param.label: Minimum number of cells per gene for RNA
param.help: Only used for joint QC if needed, assuming RNA is pre-QC'ed

param.name: max_mito_pct
param.label: Maximum percentage of mitochondrial genes
param.help: Only used for joint QC if needed, assuming RNA is pre-QC'ed

param.name: mito_prefix
param.label: Prefix for mitochondrial genes
param.help: Only used for joint QC if needed, e.g., 'MT-' for human, 'mt-' for mouse

param.name: adt_min_counts
param.label: Minimum counts per cell for ADT

param.name: use_isotype_control
param.label: Use isotype controls for DSB
param.help: Only relevant if DSB is selected

param.name: isotype_controls
param.label: Isotype control names (comma-separated)
param.help: Only relevant if DSB with isotype controls is selected

param.name: normalize_rna
param.label: Force RNA normalization
param.help: Whether to force normalization of RNA data even if it appears to be pre-processed

param.name: raw_counts_layer
param.label: Name of layer with raw counts
param.help: Only used if 'Location of raw RNA counts' is set to 'In a specific layer'

param.name: n_pcs
param.label: Number of principal components for RNA

param.name: n_latent
param.label: Number of latent dimensions for totalVI
param.help: Only relevant if totalVI is selected

param.name: max_epochs
param.label: Maximum number of training epochs for totalVI
param.help: Only relevant if totalVI is selected

param.name: gpu_device
param.label: GPU device ID for totalVI
param.help: If multiple GPUs are available, specify which one to use (0 for first GPU). Only relevant if totalVI is selected.

param.name: batch_key
param.label: Batch key for totalVI
param.help: Column name in observation metadata containing batch information (e.g., 'sample_id'). Only relevant if totalVI is selected.

param.name: continuous_covariates
param.label: Continuous covariates for totalVI
param.help: Column names in observation metadata containing continuous covariates (one name per line). Only relevant if totalVI is selected.

param.name: categorical_covariates
param.label: Categorical covariates for totalVI
param.help: Column names in observation metadata containing categorical covariates (one name per line). Only relevant if totalVI is selected.

param.name: integrated_dim_reduction_key
param.label: Integrated dimension reduction key
param.help: Key name to use for the integrated dimensionality reduction in obsm. Default is 'X_integrated', but can be changed to avoid conflicts with other reduction methods.

param.name: n_neighbors
param.label: Number of neighbors for neighborhood graph

param.name: output_format
param.label: Output format
param.option: AnnData object with protein data in obs (h5ad)

tool.help:
**CITE-Seq Analysis Pipeline**
This tool implements a comprehensive CITE-Seq analysis pipeline using the scverse ecosystem, including muon for multimodal data management and optionally scvi-tools for advanced integration.
-----
**Input Data**
The tool accepts either:
* Separate RNA and ADT count matrices (as AnnData/h5ad files) * A combined MuData object containing both RNA and ADT modalities
-----
**Pipeline Steps**
1. **Data Loading**: Load RNA and ADT data, creating a multimodal MuData object 2. **Quality Control**: Assumes RNA data has already been QC'ed, performs QC on ADT modality and aligns cells between modalities 3. **ADT Normalization**: Apply CLR or DSB normalization to ADT counts 4. **RNA Processing**: Process RNA data based on preprocessing state, identifying highly variable genes if needed 5. **Integration**: Combine RNA and ADT data using either feature concatenation or totalVI modeling 6. **Clustering**: Identify cell populations using graph-based (Leiden) clustering 7. **Visualization**: Generate UMAP embeddings for visualization
-----
**RNA Data Flexibility**
The tool is designed to work flexibly with RNA data in different preprocessing states:
* **Smart Detection**: Automatically detects if RNA data is pre-processed (has highly variable genes identified) * **Normalization Control**: Optionally skip or force normalization of RNA data * **Raw Counts for totalVI**: Provide raw counts to totalVI from one of three locations: - X matrix (default, the main expression matrix) - raw.X (raw counts backed up in .raw) - A specific layer (e.g., 'counts')
-----
**totalVI Integration Options**
The totalVI integration method provides powerful joint modeling of RNA and protein data:
* **Batch Correction**: Specify a batch key (column name in metadata) to perform batch correction * **Covariates**: Include continuous or categorical covariates in the model to account for known sources of variation * **Model Parameters**: Configure the latent space dimensions and training epochs * **Integrated Dimension Reduction Key**: Specify the key name for the integrated representation stored in obsm (default: 'X_integrated'). This can be useful to avoid conflicts with other dimensionality reduction methods like Harmony or BBKNN that might use the same key. * **Memory-efficient Raw Counts Handling**: totalVI works best with raw RNA counts. The tool will temporarily swap the raw counts from your specified location into the main expression matrix, then restore the normalized data afterward. This approach avoids duplicating the dataset in memory, allowing processing of large datasets.
**GPU Acceleration for totalVI**
When using the totalVI integration method, the tool will automatically check for GPU availability:
* If a GPU is available, the tool will use it to accelerate model training, which can significantly reduce processing time * The GPU detection is automatic and requires no user intervention * Training parameters are optimized based on available GPU memory * GPU and integration information is stored in the output MuData object's metadata
Note: For large datasets, using totalVI without GPU may result in very long processing times.
-----
**Output Options**
* **MuData object (h5mu)**: Complete multimodal object with all analysis results * **AnnData object (h5ad)**: RNA-based AnnData with protein data added to cell metadata * **Metadata table (TSV)**: Cell metadata including clustering results and protein expression
